summary: Hisao Kanaseki worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at Doshisha University from circa 1937 to 1941 and held a post at Tokyo Metropolitan University from circa 1957 to 1982.

Hisao Takahashi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Taisho University from circa 1970 to 1976 and under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He held posts at Taisho University as professor (1977–1981) and at Buzan-ha Institute of Modern Mission.

Hisashi Matsumura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at the Australian National University from circa 1980 to 1985 and served as an assistant professor at Kobe Shinwa University from circa 1988 to 1996.

Hisashi Sato specialized in Tibetology and history and archaeology. After studying at Kyoto University (circa 1934–1937), he served as professor at Kyoto University (circa 1964–1977), Bukkyo University (circa 1977–1987), Komazawa University, and Toyo University.

Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna (circa 2005–2011) under Helmut Krasser, having also studied under several teachers including Akira Saito, and became a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University circa 2017.

Hisayasu Torii worked in Sinology and linguistics after studying at Ritsumeikan University (until circa 1936) and under Yoshitaka Iriya. He taught at Xinjing Commercial School (1940–1942), Tenri University (1942–1955), and Osaka City University (1960–1969), and served with Chugokugo Gakkai.
Hitoshi Inui is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held a post as an assistant professor at Koyasan University from circa 1983 to 1997.

Hitoshi Katō specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He held positions at Otani University, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, and Nara University of Education, and became a professor at Osaka University circa 2007.

Hitoshi Obara is a scholar of history and archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Hokkaido University from circa 1963 to 1967 and served as a professor at the University of the Sacred Heart from circa 1990 to 2015.

Hjalmar Edgren was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln and under William Dwight Whitney (circa 1871–1874). He held posts at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (circa 1880–1901), Lund University, and the University of Gothenburg.

Hla Pe was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Yangon from circa 1930 to 1935 and at the University of London from circa 1937 to 1944, later teaching Gustaaf Houtman.

Ho-chin Yang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Washington (circa 1989–1994), where he studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

Ho-sung Kim specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He founded the Institute for the History of Japanese Buddhism and held a professorship at Dongguk University starting circa 1994.

Hojun Nagasaki specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (circa 1963–1965), served at Otani University (1964–2004) where he became professor emeritus, and was president of the Japanese Association for Jain Studies in 1998.

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University from circa 2003 to 2009 and took up a post at the University of Colorado Boulder circa 2008.
Holmes Welch was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Francis Woodman Cleaves and held a research post at Harvard University from circa 1963 to 1976.

Hong Luo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After doctoral studies at Peking University (circa 1999–2004), he worked at the China Tibetology Research Center (circa 2004–2017) and became a professor at Sichuan University circa 2018.

Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College from circa 1970 to 1994 and as a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Minobusan University from circa 1994 to 2011.

Hoong Teik Toh is a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Harvard University (circa 1999–2004), studying under faculty including James E. Bosson, Gray Tuttle, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Mark C. Elliott.

Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. Educated at Charterhouse School and Queens' College, Cambridge (circa 1918–1922), he served as Field Director for the Greater India Research Committee from circa 1934 to 1939.
